name: notice-rebuild-2026-10-31
purpose: Add top-of-file Apache-2.0 section 4(b) change notices to src/lib.rs and src/transform.rs inside source-patched.tar.gz, regenerate ownership.patch, and rebuild photon-owned.wasm with the pinned recipe. compact-exact-result.json and provenance.json remain the unedited 2026-10-28 proof of the previous artifact.

toolProvisioning.policy: Fresh downloads into the git-ignored vendor/photon/toolchain/ (the build.ps1 default). No tool binary, registry cache, target, source or output directory from the 2026-10-28 run was available or reused.
toolProvisioning.rust: RUSTUP_HOME=toolchain/rustup CARGO_HOME=toolchain/cargo rustup toolchain install 1.96.1-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc --profile minimal --target wasm32-unknown-unknown (rustup 1.28.2; it then reported that rustup itself is not installed in the isolated Cargo home, as REBUILD.md records for 2026-10-28)
toolProvisioning.crates: cargo build --locked against the retained Cargo.lock; 99 crates downloaded fresh from crates.io into the empty isolated Cargo home and checked against the lock's checksums by Cargo.

buildScript.difference: Line 2 only: $ErrorActionPreference='Continue' instead of 'Stop'. Under Windows PowerShell 5.1, redirecting cargo's stderr with *> under 'Stop' throws on cargo's first progress line ('Updating crates.io index'); the unmodified script failed that way. Every tool step still throws on a nonzero $LASTEXITCODE. The copy ran from vendor/photon so $PSScriptRoot, the remaps and all paths were those of build.ps1, and it was deleted afterwards.

controlRebuild.description: Unchanged 2026-10-28 source-patched.tar.gz rebuilt with the freshly downloaded tools and crates, before any source change.
controlRebuild.conclusion: The retained recipe reproduces the previous accepted artifact from fresh tool and crate downloads on this host. It is still one Windows host; cross-platform reproducibility is unproven.

sourceChange.change: Four '//' comment lines prepended to each file; no other byte of either file changed. The other 33 source files are unchanged, at the hashes compact-exact-result.json records.

sourceArchive.command: node retar-patched-source.mjs <2026-10-28 source-patched.tar.gz> <root holding the two noticed files> source-patched.tar.gz
sourceArchive.deterministic: Two runs produced identical bytes. Every other tar header and payload is copied byte-for-byte; the two replaced entries get the new size, mtime 2026-10-31T00:00:00Z and a recomputed checksum; gzip level 9, header mtime 0, OS byte 3 (Node v22.21.0, zlib 1.3.1-470d3a2).

ownershipPatch.recipe: Fresh git repository (core.autocrlf false); commit the unmodified src/lib.rs and src/transform.rs from source-unmodified.tar.gz; copy the patched files over them; git diff --no-ext-diff --abbrev=8 with diff.algorithm=myers (git 2.55.0.windows.1). The same recipe reproduces the 2026-10-28 ownership.patch byte-for-byte, and the new patch applies to the unmodified sources with patch -p1 to give exactly the noticed files.

noticeRebuild.differenceFromPrevious: 83 bytes differ, all inside 80 little-endian u32 panic-location line fields, each exactly +4. Each changed field follows a file-name length of 10 (src\lib.rs, 23 fields) or 16 (src\transform.rs, 57 fields). No other byte changed, so code, imports, exports and data layout are otherwise identical.

abiParity: vendor-photon.test.ts passes on the new artifact: every stock import and export, and every function signature, equals the installed @cf-wasm/photon 0.4.0 binary and abi-signatures.json variants.resize.abi (unchanged).
limits: The memory, parity, cold/warm and concurrency observations in the 2026-10-28 evidence and in CHANGELOG 1.3.5 were taken on the previous artifact (f848bcd2...). The byte difference above is line-number constants only, but those measurements must be re-measured on this artifact at image acceptance.
Build logs embed absolute host paths and are not retained; the compiler finish lines are recorded instead.
This proves the recipe on one Windows host with fresh downloads. Cross-platform reproducibility is unproven.
